key_insight: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem, asking whether automated machine learning engineering agents can use abundant unlabeled data alongside scarce labeled examples. The provided abstract is truncated, so it does not establish how well the approach performs.
problem_solved: Building ML systems for new domains requires costly labels and manual pipeline engineering. Existing MLE agents have largely been studied in fully supervised settings, leaving their ability to exploit unlabeled data underexplored.
method: Introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL) as a framework for studying MLE agents beyond fully supervised learning.
Frame semi-supervised learning pipeline development as a program search problem.
Focus on settings with limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data; implementation and evaluation details are unavailable in the provided excerpt.
impact: This work could guide practitioners seeking to automate ML pipeline development when labels are expensive but raw data is plentiful. Practical benefits remain unverified in the supplied excerpt.

paper_title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
paper_authors: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu, Kristin Branson, Jennifer J. Sun
